name: Anthropic Official Skills
author: anthropics
description: Official reference repository defining the open `SKILL.md` pattern, including `skill-creator`, `frontend-design`, and reusable templates for building and routing AI agent capabilities.
what_it_does: Establishes the standard `SKILL.md` directory convention where frontmatter `description` acts as a routing trigger ("Use when...") and Markdown instructions guide agent execution.
best_for: Learning the canonical `SKILL.md` structure and routing-rule best practices
Creating and iterating on custom agent skills via `skill-creator`
Bootstrapping new skills from `skills/template/SKILL.md`
verdict: EXCELLENT — the foundational reference architecture for modern `SKILL.md`-based agent ecosystems.
limitations: Primarily serves as a reference collection and template kit rather than a domain-specific tool.
Documentation reviewed; not all example skills executed locally.
risk: Maintained by Anthropic under an open-source license; still inspect individual community forks before trusting them.
installation: Browse or clone `anthropics/skills` and copy desired `SKILL.md` folders into your agent's skills directory.
notes: Essential reference whenever authoring new skills for this library.

name: VoltAgent Awesome Agent Skills
author: VoltAgent
description: A large, actively curated directory of 1,000+ open-source and official AI agent skills (`SKILL.md`) across coding, DevOps, research, and design workflows.
what_it_does: Indexes community and vendor-maintained skills with direct links, categories, and compatibility notes for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.
best_for: Discovering new candidate skills across specialized domains
Benchmarking how official teams structure `SKILL.md` repositories
Feeding new links into this library's `inbox/` evaluation pipeline
verdict: EXCELLENT — one of the best starting points on GitHub for discovering high-signal agent skills.
limitations: Directory index only; individual linked skills still require independent security and quality inspection (e.g. with `NVIDIA/SkillSpector`).
risk: Review each linked third-party skill individually before installing.
installation: Browse `VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills` on GitHub and evaluate individual skills before installing.
notes: Primary discovery source alongside `github.com/topics/agent-skills`.

name: NVIDIA Official Agent Skills
author: NVIDIA
description: NVIDIA's official portable `SKILL.md` catalog teaching AI coding agents how to work with `CUDA-X` libraries (`cuDF`, `cuOpt`), Isaac robotics, and `RAG` blueprints.
what_it_does: Syncs daily from NVIDIA product teams and provides cryptographically signed skill cards (`skill.oms.sig`) installable individually via `npx skills add` or discovered via `nvidia-skill-finder`.
best_for: Working with NVIDIA `CUDA-X`, `cuDF`, `cuOpt`, or Isaac simulation workflows
Learning enterprise-grade skill signing and provenance (`SkillEvaluator` / `SkillSpector`)
Discovering domain-specific GPU programming skills via `nvidia-skill-finder`
verdict: GOOD — high-trust, officially maintained skill catalog with strong provenance, though specialized for NVIDIA's GPU/robotics ecosystem.
limitations: Most skills target NVIDIA hardware/software stacks (`CUDA`, `Isaac`, `cuOpt`).
Repository documentation reviewed; not personally executed.
risk: Officially maintained by NVIDIA (`Apache-2.0`) with cryptographic signatures (`skill.oms.sig`).
installation: `npx skills add nvidia/skills --skill nvidia-skill-finder --yes`
notes: Pairs directly with `NVIDIA/SkillSpector` for security verification.

name: ScrapeGraphAI
author: ScrapeGraphAI
description: A Python web scraping library that uses LLM-powered graph pipelines to extract structured JSON data from websites and local documents (HTML, XML, JSON, Markdown) without brittle CSS or XPath selectors.
what_it_does: Lets you describe the target schema or information you want in natural language, then runs modular scraping graphs over web pages or local files to output structured data resilient to layout changes.
best_for: Extracting structured metadata from diverse skill directories
Converting messy HTML pages into normalized JSON records
Building repeatable Python research and data-collection pipelines
verdict: GOOD — strong option for structured metadata extraction when scraping heterogeneous pages, provided an LLM backend (local or API) is configured.
limitations: Typically requires an LLM provider (local Ollama or external API key) and Python dependencies.
Repository documentation reviewed; not personally installed or tested.
risk: Requires executing Python scraping pipelines and potentially sending fetched page text to an LLM endpoint; verify data privacy and API key handling.
installation: `pip install scrapegraphai` (see `github.com/scrapegraphai/scrapegraph-ai` for Playwright and model backend setup).
notes: Keep as an optional structured-extraction helper rather than a required dependency for SkillAtlas.

name: Scrapling MCP & One-Shot Tools
author: D4Vinci
description: An adaptive web scraping library with a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server offering stateless one-shot tools (`make_request` and `browser_fetch_once`) for extracting clean, LLM-ready content from static and JS-rendered pages.
what_it_does: Exposes `make_request` for fast HTTP fetching with browser TLS fingerprint impersonation and `browser_fetch_once` for on-demand headless browser rendering, while automatically stripping hidden HTML elements and blocking trackers to reduce prompt-injection risk.
best_for: Reading JS-heavy documentation pages and SPAs
Extracting clean Markdown/text from candidate skill repositories and docs
One-off web lookups without maintaining persistent browser sessions
Reducing prompt-injection surface when feeding web pages to agents
verdict: GOOD — very practical MCP toolset for autonomous skill investigation when standard `curl` or static fetchers hit JS-rendered pages.
limitations: Requires Python environment and optional browser dependencies for `browser_fetch_once`.
Documentation reviewed; MCP server not personally installed or executed in this environment.
risk: Fetches untrusted external web content; although it strips hidden HTML and blocks known trackers, always treat extracted page content as untrusted data.
installation: See `scrapling.readthedocs.io` for Python package and MCP server configuration instructions.
notes: Useful optional research helper for SkillAtlas inbox processing when investigating difficult documentation sites.

name: PM Skills
author: phuryn
description: A product management agent skills suite with 100+ commands and workflows covering product discovery, PRD writing, strategy, and launch planning.
what_it_does: Provides structured `SKILL.md` templates and slash-command workflows for market research, feature scoping, prioritization, and go-to-market checklists.
best_for: Drafting PRDs, product specs, and launch plans with AI agents
Structured product discovery and user-problem framing
Solo founders and PMs organizing repeatable planning workflows
verdict: GOOD — comprehensive, MIT-licensed product workflow library (`28k+` stars) filling the `business` and `productivity` gap nicely.
limitations: Focused on product/business workflows rather than code implementation.
Repository summary reviewed; not personally executed.
risk: MIT-licensed Markdown skills and workflows; low risk, review prompts before use.
installation: See `phuryn/pm-skills` on GitHub for installation instructions.
notes: Discovered via `github.com/topics/agent-skills`.

name: Alibaba Open Code Review
author: alibaba
description: An enterprise-grade hybrid code review system combining deterministic static pipelines with LLM agent skills for precise line-level PR feedback and security checks.
what_it_does: Runs deterministic diff/AST checks alongside modular agent skills to catch bugs, style violations, and security issues directly on pull requests.
best_for: Automated pull request review and security gating
Combining deterministic linters with LLM reasoning
Large team code-review workflows
verdict: GOOD — strong hybrid architecture (`56k+` stars, `Apache-2.0`, actively maintained) that avoids pure-LLM review noise.
limitations: Heavier setup than lightweight prompt-only review skills like `ponytail`.
Repository summary reviewed; not personally deployed.
risk: Apache-2.0 open-source project; review CI/CD webhook tokens and LLM provider configuration.
installation: See `alibaba/open-code-review` on GitHub for CLI and CI setup.
notes: Discovered via `github.com/topics/agent-skills`.

name: Ponytail
author: dietrichgebert
description: Forces AI coding agents to climb a strict "Decision Ladder" before writing new code, preventing over-engineering and unnecessary dependencies. Encourages reusing existing codebase helpers, standard library features, and native platform capabilities first.
what_it_does: Provides a portable `SKILL.md` / `AGENTS.md` instruction set with adjustable intensity modes (`lite`, `full`, `ultra`) and companion audit/review commands (`/ponytail-review`, `/ponytail-audit`) to keep generated diffs minimal while preserving error handling, security, and accessibility.
best_for: Preventing AI agents from over-engineering simple features
Auditing bloated pull requests or diffs
Enforcing codebase reuse and minimal-code discipline
Multi-agent setups across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI
verdict: EXCELLENT — directly addresses one of the biggest failure modes of AI coding assistants (unnecessary complexity and boilerplate) with a clear, practical decision framework.
limitations: Effectiveness depends on the host model faithfully following system/skill instructions.
Public documentation and summaries reviewed; not personally executed in a live session.
risk: Pure instruction-based skill (`SKILL.md` / `AGENTS.md`); review the exact prompt text before adding to global agent rules to ensure it does not conflict with project-specific architecture mandates.
installation: See the original GitHub repository (`dietrichgebert/ponytail`) for `SKILL.md` / `AGENTS.md` placement instructions.
notes: Core principle ("lazy about the solution, never lazy about reading") is directly applied in this repository's own scripts and UI architecture.

name: NVIDIA SkillSpector
author: NVIDIA
description: Open-source security scanner by NVIDIA that audits third-party AI agent skills, `SKILL.md` repos, and `MCP` servers for prompt injection, data exfiltration, and malicious code before installation.
what_it_does: Combines fast static analysis (AST inspection, regex, `YARA` rules, taint tracking, and `OSV.dev` vulnerability checks) with an optional LLM semantic evaluation layer to catch hidden risks and reduce false positives.
best_for: Auditing untrusted `SKILL.md` or `MCP` servers before adding them to your environment
Detecting prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or dangerous `eval`/`exec` patterns
Integrating automated skill security gates via `skillspector-action` in GitHub Actions
verdict: EXCELLENT — essential security guardrail for anyone collecting and testing third-party AI skills.
limitations: Optional LLM semantic layer requires configuring a model endpoint.
Public repository documentation reviewed; CLI not personally executed in this workspace.
risk: Security auditing tool by NVIDIA (`Apache-2.0`); safe to inspect and run in CI/local environments.
installation: See `NVIDIA/SkillSpector` on GitHub for CLI and `skillspector-action` setup instructions.
notes: Great companion to this library's `security` audit workflow before marking any skill `verified`.

name: Superpowers
author: obra
description: An agentic software engineering framework that enforces `TDD`, `systematic-debugging`, `brainstorming`, and `writing-plans` through composable `SKILL.md` modules so coding agents work like disciplined engineers.
what_it_does: Bootstraps agents with a `using-superpowers` routing discipline that requires checking and following structured `SKILL.md` workflows before writing code or answering implementation questions.
best_for: Enforcing test-driven development and root-cause debugging
Breaking complex features into explicit `writing-plans` and `executing-plans` steps
Authoring new skills with `writing-skills` TDD checks
verdict: EXCELLENT — one of the most structured, battle-tested agent workflow skill suites for serious software engineering.
limitations: Adds workflow overhead for trivial one-line edits unless scoped appropriately.
Public repository documentation reviewed; not personally executed as a standalone plugin.
risk: Pure Markdown skill instructions and workflow rules; review bootstrap hooks before enabling globally.
installation: See the `obra/superpowers` GitHub repository for plugin/skill installation instructions.
notes: Pair with `ponytail` to combine disciplined TDD/debugging workflows with minimal-code restraint.

name: AntiSlopUI
author: Vanszs
description: A UI/UX steering-skill framework that stops AI coding agents from generating generic, formulaic "AI slop" interfaces. Combines a deterministic ban filter against cliché layouts with a positive pattern library and design-system token guidance.
what_it_does: Supplies a core `SKILL.md` steering file, cliché pattern bans, curated `references/` layout patterns, a CSV design-system generator, and a `ui-ux-pro-max/` audit tool to enforce intentional typography, color restraint, and accessible component hierarchy.
best_for: Frontend web applications and developer tools
Avoiding generic SaaS hero templates and rainbow gradients
Establishing consistent design tokens and typography
Auditing existing UIs for polish and accessibility
verdict: EXCELLENT — one of the most practical UI steering frameworks for turning default LLM frontend output into deliberate, production-grade interfaces.
limitations: Requires the coding agent to load and respect the reference files during UI generation.
Public repository structure and documentation reviewed; not personally executed via its CLI/audit scripts.
risk: Primarily Markdown rules and local design reference scripts; inspect any included helper scripts before running them locally.
installation: See the `Vanszs/AntiSlopUI` GitHub repository for skill installation and `references/` setup.
notes: Used as the primary design philosophy for SkillAtlas: restrained palette, crisp borders, information-dense cards, and zero generic marketing fluff.

name: Hallmark
author: nutlope
description: A purpose-built UI/UX design skill by Nutlope that replaces generic AI "template slop" with curated visual themes, intentional typography, and automated browser linting (`sloplint`).
what_it_does: Provides structured modes including `/hallmark redesign`, `/hallmark audit`, and `Study` alongside dozens of visual themes and Puppeteer-based multi-viewport checks to catch layout flaws and AI UI clichés.
best_for: Redesigning existing web apps with cohesive typography and deliberate color systems
Running `/hallmark audit` to catch generic AI UI anti-patterns
Extracting design DNA from reference URLs or screenshots
verdict: EXCELLENT — pairs strong thematic design craft with automated browser-level visual linting (`sloplint`).
limitations: Automated `sloplint` checks require a local Node/Puppeteer browser environment.
Public repository documentation reviewed; not personally executed via CLI.
risk: MIT-licensed skill package; review skill prompts and scripts before running globally.
installation: `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g`
notes: Used alongside `AntiSlopUI` to guide SkillAtlas's visual redesign (editorial typography, crisp surfaces, and semantic highlighters).

name: HeyGen HyperFrames
author: heygen-com
description: HeyGen's open-source AI video editor for people and agents that turns HTML/code compositions into frame-accurate `MP4` videos using headless Chrome and `FFmpeg`.
what_it_does: Lets coding agents write or edit declarative HTML/CSS/JS video scenes and render them deterministically frame-by-frame, with visual inspection in *HyperFrames Studio*.
best_for: Programmatic YouTube explainers, product demos, and motion graphics
Frame-accurate AI video editing controlled by code rather than opaque video models
Integrating video rendering directly into Claude Code or Cursor workflows
verdict: EXCELLENT — deterministic HTML-to-MP4 rendering gives coding agents full frame-level control over video output.
limitations: Requires headless Chrome and `FFmpeg` in the local rendering environment.
Public repository documentation reviewed; not personally rendered locally.
risk: Apache-2.0 open-source project; inspect generated scripts and local `FFmpeg` / Chrome dependencies.
installation: `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`
notes: Strong choice for code-driven YouTube and product demo video pipelines.

name: Hypit
author: hypit-ai
description: An open-source agent framework and markup language for parsing reference videos into word-anchored workflows (`captions`, `B-roll`, `effects`) to clone or localize video formats.
what_it_does: Converts a reference or viral video into structured word-anchored timeline markup rather than a flat script, letting AI agents swap voiceovers, faces, text, or assets cleanly.
best_for: Cloning high-performing short-form or YouTube Shorts video structures
Creating localized or A/B-tested variations of existing videos
Word-anchored caption and B-roll timing workflows
verdict: PROMISING — clever word-anchored video markup approach for format cloning and variations; license and local setup need verification.
limitations: License listed as non-standard/unknown (`NOASSERTION` on GitHub).
Repository summary reviewed; not personally tested on video files.
risk: Review licensing terms and any media-processing binaries/API keys before production use.
installation: See `hypit-ai/hypit` on GitHub for installation and agent skill setup.
notes: Useful for YouTube Shorts / Reels format iteration when paired with `youtube-agent-skill`.

name: OpenMontage
author: OpenMontageInc
description: An open-source agentic video production system featuring 100+ tools and hundreds of skill/knowledge files that turn coding assistants into an end-to-end video studio.
what_it_does: Orchestrates multi-stage video pipelines—from scriptwriting and asset generation to editing and final synthesis—directly through natural language prompts in your IDE.
best_for: End-to-end automated video creation inside Claude Code or Cursor
Multi-step YouTube and social video production pipelines
Exploring large-scale agent skill & tool orchestration patterns
verdict: GOOD — comprehensive agentic video production suite with strong community adoption, though `AGPL-3.0` licensing and multi-tool setup require attention.
limitations: Large surface area (100+ tools) may require significant setup and external media model keys.
Licensed under `AGPL-3.0`; check compatibility for commercial SaaS use.
Documentation reviewed; not personally executed.
risk: Review tool permissions and external API/model dependencies before running automated pipelines.
installation: See `OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage` on GitHub for workspace setup instructions.
notes: Compare with `hyperframes` (deterministic HTML) and `video-shotcraft` (Remotion) depending on your video style.

name: Pixelle-Video
author: ATH-MaaS
description: An automated AI short-video engine by `ATH-MaaS` that generates scripts, AI images, voice narration, and background music from a single text topic using `ComfyUI` and multiple LLMs.
what_it_does: Connects LLMs (`GPT`, `Qwen`, `DeepSeek`, `Ollama`) with `ComfyUI` image pipelines and TTS/audio synthesis to produce vertical or horizontal short videos from topic prompts.
best_for: Automated faceless YouTube Shorts, TikTok, or Reels generation
Local or hybrid `Ollama` + `ComfyUI` video workflows
Batch short-video prototyping from topic lists
verdict: GOOD — practical end-to-end short-video generator with `ComfyUI` integration and flexible LLM support.
limitations: Requires `ComfyUI` and model weights/API keys for image, voice, and LLM steps.
Last pushed `2026-06-14`; check recent issue activity before adopting.
Not personally executed.
risk: Apache-2.0 licensed; verify custom `ComfyUI` nodes and model downloads from trusted sources.
installation: See `ATH-MaaS/Pixelle-Video` on GitHub for `ComfyUI` and Python setup.
notes: Good fit for faceless content automation workflows.

name: Toonflow App
author: HBAI-Ltd
description: An open-source AI video creation platform for short dramas, comic videos (`manju`), and animated storytelling using an infinite canvas workspace and AI agents.
what_it_does: Parses raw story text, manages character and scene consistency assets, generates outlines and storyboards, and orchestrates multi-provider AI image and video generation with local deployment support.
best_for: Animated storytelling, comic-style videos, and short drama production
Consistent character and scene asset management across episodes
Teams wanting an infinite-canvas storyboard workflow
verdict: PROMISING — well-starred MIT-licensed visual storyboarding and animation platform; best suited for narrative/comic video rather than general coding workflows.
limitations: Requires configuring external or local image/video generation providers.
Repository documentation reviewed; not personally deployed.
risk: MIT-licensed open-source project; inspect provider API configurations before local deployment.
installation: See `HBAI-Ltd/Toonflow-app` on GitHub for local deployment instructions.
notes: Interesting reference for multi-agent storyboarding and character consistency.

name: Video Shotcraft
author: Vincentwei1021
description: An AI video skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns product pages or specs into editable, cinematic promotional videos built with `Remotion`.

best_for: Product launch demos, SaaS promo videos, and UI showcase reels
Clean, editable `Remotion` motion graphics driven by coding agents
Beat-synced promotional edits with deterministic text rendering
verdict: GOOD — practical `Remotion`-based video skill with 150+ shot recipes and crisp typography/UI rendering.
limitations: Focuses on code-driven `Remotion` compositions rather than photorealistic AI video.
Repository summary reviewed; not personally rendered locally.
risk: Apache-2.0 licensed; inspect `Remotion` dependencies and media assets before building.
installation: See `Vincentwei1021/video-shotcraft` on GitHub for skill and `Remotion` setup.
notes: Complements `hyperframes` if you prefer React + `Remotion` over raw HTML/FFmpeg compositions.

name: Spicy API Skills

Niche 18+ scope; not relevant for general coding or content workflows.

High-rigor research skill architecture inspiration
